tagline: A hundred miles down a river that became three lakes.
intro: From Oakway in Oconee County the byway strings state highways together and keeps to the South Carolina side of the Savannah River, down past Calhoun Falls and through McCormick, to the Georgia line below Clarks Hill. Along the way the river has become three Army Corps lakes, Hartwell, Russell and Thurmond, a chain about 120 miles long.
Russell, the newest, is kept within five feet of full pool, so it always looks full, and its shore is almost wholly undeveloped. Near Thurmond the road passes through Sumter National Forest.

moments.title: Richard B. Russell Lake
moments.text: Before the water rose in 1983 crews dug the plantation, fort and mound sites it would cover. The old Georgia-Carolina Memorial Bridge was simply left, and stands intact beneath the lake.

moments.title: McCormick
moments.text: William Dorn took nearly a million dollars in gold from his mine here in the 1850s. Cyrus McCormick bought it in 1869, searched until 1882, then sold the land for a town.

moments.title: Lake Strom Thurmond
moments.text: A clerical slip made it Clark Hill. Strom Thurmond's bill later put the s back, and in 1988 Congress gave it his own name. Georgia still calls it Clarks Hill.
